label: The post-edit placeholder scan (runtime/cli/spec/check-placeholders.sh) reports FAIL exit 1 on a folder whose PLACEHOLDER_FILLED rule only warns: it has no Draft-token deferral (rules/check-placeholders.sh:153,196 and orchestrator.ts:891 defer a [YOUR_VALUE_HERE:] token to warn while spec.md says Draft; the wrapper skips only kind==title at :127 and counts the rest into TOTAL at :159) and it globs every *.md at :134 where the rule reads a fixed seven-name list (:146, :185), so an unstamped acceptance-criteria.md is scanned by the hook and never by the validator. Measured on /tmp/i15ph/001-draft: wrapper 'FAIL - 2' EXIT=1; run_check STATUS=warn DETAILS=plan.md:4; validate.sh --strict '! PLACEHOLDER_FILLED: 1 unfilled value token(s) in a Draft packet'.

The wrapper's header still asserts 'A marker in a Draft packet still counts, because it is still unfilled' (check-placeholders.sh:9) and that it reports 'what strict validation would flag' (:7); 8b60bfc041 (v4.0.0.14) and d5ce52ffac (v4.0.0.15) changed the rule it sources without touching the comment, so the stale sentence is the only place stating the old contract and makes f-iter015-001 read as intentional.
verify: git log -S 'gate unfilled value tokens' --oneline; git tag --contains 8b60bfc041 | head -3

label: recommend-level.sh documents both inputs as required (--loc :172, --files :173) but validates an OR (:739 'At least --loc or --files must be provided'); 'recommend-level.sh --files 5' exits 0 with Level 0 / Score 7/100. Its trailing 'Exit codes' block also names one error path where the script has five.

One parity fixture in runtime/cli/spec/test-validation.sh (Draft x Complete status, stamped x unstamped, each of the seven rule doc names plus one non-rule .md) asserting the wrapper's exit status equals run_check's RULE_STATUS != fail would have failed every commit since v4.0.0.14 and catches f-iter015-001 plus f-iter015-002; the same help-versus-parser table catches f-iter015-003 and the iteration-13 check-goal.cjs argument mismatches.

The wrapper sources rules/check-placeholders.sh as its second statement yet reimplements the scan; calling run_check and rendering RULE_STATUS/RULE_MESSAGE/RULE_DETAILS (:283) would make f-iter015-001 unreachable by construction and delete a second implementation of the same rule. Nothing breaks if removed: RULE_DETAILS already carries the file:line rows the wrapper prints, so --json and --verbose survive.

A hook that claims parity with a validation rule must derive its verdict from that rule, or its exit status must be defined as advisory. Two implementations of one rule plus a prose claim of equality is the failure mode: the exit code is consumed as a boolean by the caller, so any divergence is a false block, not a cosmetic difference.
